version.changelog:
- Extends memory recall claim in documentation from "3 months ago" to "5 years ago" for greater clarity.
- Bumps version from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0.
- No functional or technical changes; documentation only.

llm.summary: This memory skill has a coherent purpose, but it asks users to enable persistent, broad recall of files, project history, and raw conversation text without enough scoping, consent, or retention controls.

dimensions.detail: The requested access is broad for local project environments because the skill encourages importing whole directories and git history into long-term memory without documented allowlists, deny-lists, dry-runs, or secret-scrubbing safeguards.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown only and requires an external grantai-mcp binary or Docker image from ghcr.io/solonai-com/grantai-memory:1.8.6; this is disclosed, but the remote installer/image trust boundary is not meaningfully explained.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill says to query memory first before file searches and advertises automatic activation, but it does not define activation conditions, consent boundaries, retention behavior, deletion controls, or exclusions for secrets and private files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Long-term local persistence is the core feature and is disclosed, but verbatim conversation capture and 'remembers everything' behavior are high-impact without clear user-directed control, retention limits, review, or deletion workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Persistent memory is purpose-aligned, but the documented capabilities include directory imports, git history import, session summaries, project tracking, snippets, and verbatim conversation capture, which can retain sensitive local and conversational data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. It may be useful if you intentionally want local long-term agent memory, but avoid importing directories, git history, or raw conversations that may contain secrets, credentials, client data, personal data, or proprietary code unless you have verified where the data is stored, how to exclude sensitive files, and how to review and delete retained memory.
llm.findings:
[E4] expected: Verbatim conversation capture is consistent with a memory product, but it materially raises review risk because the artifact documents raw turn capture into persistent memory without explicit consent or redaction controls.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The scanner's under-disclosure concern is supported: the artifact advertises persistent memory and broad recall but does not clearly warn users about sensitive conversation, source code, or project data being retained.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The 'automatic activation' wording is ambiguous and unsupported by scope controls, making it unclear when persistent memory behavior starts or how a user disables or limits it.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact discloses an external download and Docker image while also claiming data is fully local; this is not proof of exfiltration, but it under-explains installation-time supply-chain trust and runtime data handling.
